newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia frees some arrested after rioting.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia frees some arrested after rioting.

text.p: Indonesian judges ordered on Wednesday the release of 59 people arrested after riots in Jakarta four months ago but many of them will appeal against partial convictions, supporters and court officials said.
They said judges in the Central Jakarta State Court acquitted seven of the accused and sentenced 52 others to time already served in custody.

The verdicts comprised half of the 10 judgments due on Wednesday on the fate of 124 supporters of opposition figure Megawati Sukarnoputri, who were taken into custody after police raided the headquarters of the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) on July 27.
The raid led to riots in Jakarta in which at least five people died. It was the worst violence in the city for more than two decades.

The judges in the five cases acquitted all accused on charges of assault but found that all but seven were guilty of disobeying police orders to vacate the headquarters. They were each sentenced to four months' prison.
Megawati's supporters had taken over the building after she was ousted from the PDI leadership by a government-backed faction in June.
In one courtroom, the accused rushed toward the bench shouting "It was engineered", but defence lawyers restrained them from approaching the judge after he read out the verdict, witnesses said.
Riot police then entered the courtroom and escorted the judge out. They stayed on for the other cases.
Chief defence lawyer R.O. Tambunan said those convicted would appeal in the High Court.
Megawati, the daughter of late founding president Sukarno, was in one of the courtrooms and listened to the verdict calmly.
Court officials said the accused would be taken back to prison and released later in the day.
Political analysts have said the government moved to sideline Megawati and her supporters because they feared she could draw votes from the ruling Golkar party in next year's parliamentary elections.
Megawati has also filed a lawsuit against the Election Institute for rejecting her application to file a list of candidates for the polls.

Indonesia permits only three parties to contest elections -- Golkar, the PDI and the Moslem-oriented United Development Party. It has said Megawati does not represent the PDI and has allowed the rival faction to present a list of election candidates.
